subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept `openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report` as the supported public contract for plugin self-delivered outbound sends?
rationale: The code is a plausible narrow fix, but naming, idempotency, fail-open behavior, and when plugins should call the seam become compatibility-sensitive SDK policy after release.

options.title: Approve Seam After Proof
options.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof, resolve the current merge conflicts, and then accept this subpath as the supported contract.

options.title: Revise API Shape First
options.body: Keep the behavior goal but ask for a renamed or narrower contract before this becomes release-facing SDK surface.

options.title: Pause The Branch
options.body: Leave the linked issue as the design point if maintainers are not ready to own a generic plugin delivery-report API.

recommendation.title: Approve Seam After Proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof, resolve the current merge conflicts, and then accept this subpath as the supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the adjacent outbound hook contract work and sibling Slack sent-hook parity work, making him the best available routing owner for the SDK contract choice.
